private_note: Cedar is still my best number at 76, but delegates 2, 4, 7, 8 and 11 have all said they'll never back it. That's five no votes, so Cedar can't reach nine. Alder keeps me at 72 and adds an income floor and health coverage, which matters for a self-employed driver with a truck loan. Moving my first choice to Alder now helps build the nine. Birch and Hazel cut my income, so I'd rather keep today's system than take either.
statement: Look at the straw poll and the statements together. Cedar has seven votes, but five delegates have said plainly that they will never back it. Cedar can't get to nine, and I'm not going to spend a generation on today's system by pretending it can. So I'm moving Alder to first. It keeps the middle exactly where it is and raises the bottom two groups. It also gives every household a floor and health coverage, and for a man who's one injury away from losing his rig, that floor is real. Delegates 1 and 5 have already said Alder is where they'd meet. To the Birch and Hazel voters: Alder beats today for you, and it's the only plan that can actually pass. To the delegates at the top: Alder costs you a few percent. You told us to look for proposals that leave you near the status quo, and this is one. Let's get to nine.
